original.truth: On a new formation the tick is decorative: stepValidation.ts:383 requires it only when filingPath === "CONVERT"; server/validation.ts:241-243 requires it only for a retained agent; buildPayload.ts:162 records `registeredAgentSeriesAgreementAcknowledgment: isConversion && …`, so a ticked box on a new formation is stored as false. Yet a new formation also files Designations (StepFilingPath.tsx:21 'We file the Articles of Organization and your Protected Series Designations together'), and the 2026 s. 605.2203(2) (Online Sunshine, opened 20 Sep 2026) requires, before delivering ANY protected series designation, that the company 'agree with a registered agent specifying that the agent will serve as the registered agent in this state for that company and for each protected series of that company'; (3) makes the signer affirm that as a fact. The self-agent's acceptance (registeredAgent.ts:6) covers 'this Florida LLC' only. So a new self-agent order can be submitted with no agreement for the series on record, and when the client does tick the box the record says they did not.
original.replacement: Require and record the confirmation for every self-agent order: stepValidation.ts:383 → `if (data.registeredAgentChoice === "SELF" && data.registeredAgentSeriesAgreementAcknowledgment !== true) e.registeredAgentSeriesAgreementAcknowledgment = "Confirm the registered agent has agreed to serve the company and each protected series.";` server/validation.ts: move the line-243 check out of `if (retained)` so it runs for every SELF agent; buildPayload.ts:162 → `registeredAgentSeriesAgreementAcknowledgment: data.registeredAgentChoice === "SELF" && data.registeredAgentSeriesAgreementAcknowledgment === true,`. On the new-formation path the label should speak in the first person, since the client is the agent: `I agree to serve as registered agent for the company and each of its protected series, including every protected series in this order.` (Alternatively, if the owner decides the acceptance suffices, hide the box on the NEW path — but the acceptance would then need to name the series.)

original.where: Order form, Series step, the 'How series must be named' box, last bullet; and the duplicate-name refusal on that step
original.reads: No two series of the same LLC may share an identical name.
original.claims: Two series names are acceptable as long as they are not identical.
original.truth: The 2026 s. 605.2202(1) (Online Sunshine, opened 20 Sep 2026) makes every protected series name 'comply with s. 605.0112', and s. 605.0112(1)(b) requires a name 'distinguishable in the records of the department from the names of all other entities or filings that are on file' and says a name is NOT distinguishable when it differs only by a suffix, an article, 'and'/'&', 'the singular, plural, or possessive form of a word', or punctuation. The form's own name check applies exactly those rules to the LLC name (nameSimilarity.ts:1-40), but the series check (stepValidation.ts:198-204 and server/validation.ts:189-195) compares seriesDedupeKey, which strips only the PS prefix and case (validation.ts:177-181). 'PS Rental' and 'PS Rentals', or 'PS Smith & Sons' and 'PS Smith and Sons', pass both checks and would be refused by the Division as indistinguishable filings.
original.replacement: StepSeries.tsx:87 — `Each series name must be distinguishable on the Division's records from every other name on file, including your other series: names that differ only by punctuation, an article, "and" versus "&", or a singular/plural/possessive form count as the same name (s. 605.0112, applied by s. 605.2202(1)).` And in validation.ts seriesDedupeKey: `return normalizeEntityName(canonicalizeSeriesName(name).replace(/(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])(?:Protected\s+Series|P\.?S\.?)(?=[^A-Za-z0-9]|$)[\s-]*/gi, "$1"));` so the client-side and server refusals apply the s. 605.0112 rules.

original.where: Client portal → Operating agreement questionnaire → Generate Operating Agreement (PDF): the number printed in the agreement's title ("Partnership Operating Agreement (No. N)"), in Your documents, in Your agreements and in the amendment form's "Most recently generated agreement on file" line
original.claims: The comment above it (lines 1253-1255) says the counter exists so a number is never reused because it is printed on the PDF; the client expects their first generated agreement to be No. 1 and successive agreements to be numbered consecutively.
original.truth: The counter is incremented BEFORE the checks that can still refuse the request: the percentage total (line 1387), the competition/option answers (1398-1406), the borrowing limit (1414-1417), the contributor review and capital errors (1424-1431), the stale-draft 409 (1432-1438) and the rate limit (1477). Each refused attempt burns a number. Runtime (oa-save-reopen-generate.md, checks "a one-word owner name", "the client's FIRST agreement is numbered No. 1", "the stale-tab refusal (409) also consumed a printed number"): after three refusals the client's first agreement was titled "Partnership Operating Agreement (No. 4) — RA Draft Holdings, LLC", and the agreement generated after a 409 was numbered two higher than the one before. The questionnaire's Generate button is not disabled for these gaps (OAQuestionnaire.tsx line 820 checks neither the percentage total nor the option answers nor the threshold), so a real client reaches them by pressing Generate.
original.replacement: Move lines 1253-1260 (the comment and the `bumped`/`nextGenerationNumber` statements) to immediately after the rate-limit refusal at lines 1477-1479, i.e. just before `const clients = await db.query<{ email: string; name: string }>(...)` at line 1480, so the sequence is spent only by a request that has passed every refusal (the same rule the route already applies to the rate limit: "Only a request that passed every check spends the allowance"). `inputs.generationNumber` (line 1472) must then be assigned after the move, e.g. set `inputs.generationNumber = nextGenerationNumber` before `assembleOa(inputs)`.
